what: L1 B6: the language spells are drawn in (docs/design/LOOK_BIBLE.md rule 13). Per school: stepped bands on a 1D heat gradient (edge, mid, core in rising heat; t = the heat a band starts at, from MB5's area shares of the body), each band's color (Oklab L, C, h and hex: the displayed color it is FROM) and emit (the linear gain that lands it there through the night rig's exposure, AgX and grade, calibrated on the lookdev stage); a soft outer glow; painted sparks. Read by logic/Look/FxLanguage.cs; drawn by shaders/fx_cel.gdshaderinc. Written by tools/style/fx_measure.py build (re-run after moving a box); emit and t_tuned are the stage's and survive a rebuild.

wave.what: r3 fix 2: every ring's wavefront (p7_wave): painted arcs about arc_px long at the reach (3-9 a ring), dust shed off them as the front passes each share of its reach (shed), dust_px the puffs at the play camera; open_deg the charge stop's forward arc

glint.what: the press on every move: one three-band glint at the blade tip or shield, plus a dust kick

ring.what: the target: a wavefront standing at the hit radius; arcs grow to its coverage curve (s since the press), opacity with them; one flash at 1.5x width when shut

ribbon.what: the blade's path through the air, splined; blade: the share of the blade's own swing over her chest's arc

crack.what: px at the dark gap; gap: the crack strip's gap as a share of its band (art/fx/longcut crack_albedo, ~0.1); the seam the light down its middle

crescent.what: the press: the crescent flash on the shield

star.what: one per hit at the contact

stop.what: the champion stops her: one star and one wavefront off the shield

hit_budget.what: P7 lead 7 (main's ruling, 10 Nov): one source (the hits of one art and school in one frame) that lands more than n hits shows only n of them: crits take the places first (the n nearest her when there are more crits than places), plain hits fill the rest nearest the middle of what was struck (the blade's contact for the held cut, else the centroid). A hushed hit, plain or crit, throws no hit burst, no crit burst and no gore chips (logic/Look/HitBudget.cs, src/Fx/BattleFx.cs HitSparkBudget). A source of n hits or fewer is untouched; numbers and a kill's gore are never touched. The hushed hits land as one shared impact: camera trauma shake_per for each hushed hit, at most shake_cap (and the held cut's contact mark grows with the bodies struck: grip.contact).
hit_budget.shake_doc: Every hit's camera shake is RAISED TO a trauma, never summed (BattleFx.HitShake; main's px targets, 10 Nov). Shake at her is at most 19.2 px x trauma^2 (mean 10), trauma falls 0.0233 a frame and once before it is drawn. px below: tools numbers over every noise phase (scratch_skills_p7/l8/shake_felt.py).
hit_budget.crit_shake_doc: ANY crit in the game (not only the held cut's): trauma raised to this. Target: a lone crit is a tick, about 1 px for a frame or two. 0.24 = 0.89 px worst phase, 0.49 median, never a frame above 1 px, under 0.5 px by frame +3 at the latest. A steady stream of crits holds it there (0.47 px mean, 0.89 worst) and never builds.
hit_budget.shake_per_doc: The shared impact of a cut's hushed hits: trauma raised to shake_per x hushed, capped at shake_cap. Target: the cap is reached near 100 hushed (about 35 bodies), and a cut through 1-3 bodies (0-5 hushed, 0.0325 at most) adds nothing a crit would not, so it stays under 1 px.
hit_budget.shake_cap_doc: Target: a cut through about 37 bodies peaks 4-6 px at her and is under 0.5 px inside about 20 frames. 0.65 = peak 4.8 px median (3.5-6.2 for 8 phases in 10, 7.5 worst), 13 frames above 1 px, under 0.5 px from frame +18 (median), +20 (worst).
hit_budget.grip_shake_doc: The held cut's own contact, camera trauma RAISED TO this (BattleFx.HitShake: never a sum; shake px at her is at most 19.2 x trauma^2). Target: a cut alone is nothing (under 0.05 px at her, one or two frames). grip_shake = a Sunder cut that struck (was 0.04 + 0.02 as two sums, three times over in a three-arc swing), grip_shake_air = a Sunder cut through air, grip_shake_oath = an Oathblade cut that struck (a third of Sunder's, as before).

grip.what: P7 lead 9, the held swing's arc, TAKE 7 (src/Fx/BattleFx.Grip.cs, logic/Look/GripPaint.cs, shaders/fx_grip_stroke.gdshader): ONE brush stroke of paint laid by the sword: one mesh, one material, one draw. THE PRESS IS LAID, NOT CARRIED: every rib stores its own press and whiteness when the blade lays it (grip.press), the contact presses the ribs round the crossing once, in place; the head is a brush CAP ahead of the blade (grip.cap); the body is brushed in lanes (grip.fill); the contact splays tines (grip.splay) and throws streaks to the cut's reach (grip.throw); its white is its own (grip.white). px at the play camera, m in the world, s of real time. lead_frames, slow, snap as before; min_len = the least path drawn (m: a stroke is born on its first drawn frame as the cap and a point); face = [under this share of the blade's line showing across the path on screen the ribbon is turned wholly to the camera, above this it is the blade's own sweep]; point = the tail: [its first m from the drawn tail run to a point, the power]; retract = the leaving's clock (gone at 1); shed_at = s after the contact [the whole stroke starts thinning toward the tip's path, it is at shed_to of its width].
grip._doc_birth_sweep: rad the tip must have gone round her, the cut's way, over a run of cutting samples before that run is a stroke (GripPaint.Run): the blade lifting from rest into the swing is fast but does not sweep (it drew a squared chip a frame before the stroke). Once born the stroke's start is kept: nothing laid is dropped.
grip.kink_what: (round 4, lead 8) THE RIBBON NEVER LIES OVER ITSELF ON SCREEN. kink = [the share of a rib kept up to where it would cross another on screen (the stroke is held inside the turn: it pinches at a sharp kink); a rib held under this share of the stroke's own width there is a KINK; the metres SEEN the part after the kink must be before the part before it runs out (a stroke of its own, never a blink; until then the kink is a clean mitre)]. kink_run = how far the part BEFORE the last kink has run out toward it, by drawn frame since the path first kinked (the edge-on part sheds first: one stroke after the kink, not an L).

sunder.what: head = the stroke's width at press 1 (a share of the blade, in from the tip's path); max_len = the longest drawn (m); flash = the contact's size

contact.what: (take 7) the contact is the stroke's own PRESS: on the frame the blade crosses the struck body (wait_frames at most for the crossing; k_min = the least share up the blade the log's point sits) the ribs laid round the crossing are pressed once (grip.press.contact) and stay. Size: by_struck = [distinct bodies at the cap, the size there (x one body's)], x kill for a kill, never past the cap, x the weapon's flash. grit = the heavy blade's dust puffs (0).

link.what: on = 0: the thread and the hot edge are not drawn (the single cut is judged without them; the next solver rebuilds the turn). A chain: the next cut inside window s of the last contact, the grip still held. Opposite side and its start within max_gap m of the last cut's end: its tail is a thread from that end through a turn hook (hook m past the end, hook_w m wide when the two points meet) into its first fast sample. along = the brush's along on the thread.

edge.what: the hot edge between a chain's cuts: a core line px wide on the real blade, a glint_px star at its tip, lifted lift m toward the camera; steps out gold then amber, out_frames each, when the chain breaks

press._doc: (take 7, ii) THE PRESS IS LAID. A rib's press (x the look's head = its width) is stored when the blade lays it and never moves along the stroke. rise = [m SEEN from the stroke's start over which the press rises (the brush lands: a pointed start), its power, the press at the very start]; lift = [the tip's m/s under which the brush has lifted, at which it is whole, the press's share when lifted] (the blade slowing at the swing's end: the stroke tapers at both ends); contact = [the press added at size 1 where the blade crossed the bodies, its reach toward the head (m), toward the tail (m), the whiteness added at size 1]; hold = the raise's share by drawn frame of the RIB's own age since it was pressed (whole for three: the thick section stays where it was laid while the head moves on; it only settles, never to nothing: the finished stroke is fattest at the contact); white = m seen from the start over which a rib's whiteness rises 0 to 1 (amber, gold, then white: the tail's colors are laid, not carried). (take 8) rise[2] is high: the brush LANDS LOADED (frame 1 is a comma: a round head, the tail's point is grip.point's); the contact's raise is local and at most about 1.4x its neighbours (sunder.head 0.46: the body is a stroke, not a sail); loaded = the head is white for this many m behind the blade's line whatever was laid there.

grip._doc_cap: (take 7, i) THE HEAD IS A BRUSH CAP AHEAD OF THE BLADE, in stroke widths at the head: cap = [its length past the blade's line along the path's tangent, the nose's place across (0 the tip's path, 1 the inner edge), how far BEHIND the blade's line the inner edge starts, the outer corner's round-off (share of the length), the inner curve's power (under 1: concave: a fang), the inner edge's further retreat at the shed's end (vi: the head closes to a point)]. cap_rag = the cap's edge is bristle tips: [a bristle px across, the tips' variation (m), a tip's rounding (share of the bristle)].

fill._doc: (take 7, iii) THE BODY IS BRUSHED. lanes = bristle lanes across the width (uneven); (take 8) share = a lane's share of its length [at the stroke's white, up to the second value; the rest the third] (each lane changes value in streaks along the sweep, hard ends); values_day / values_night = the second and the third value as the white x [r, g, b, r, g, b] in sRGB: FAR ENOUGH APART TO READ at 1:1 (take 7's 0.93 / 0.85 in linear could not be seen); gold = the inner edge's band [its share of the width (the innermost lanes are gold), the light gold's green x the gold's, the next lane's share in gold (the band's border steps in and out)]; press = THE PRESS IS MORE PAINT [the values' shares shift toward the deeper ones by this at the raise's most, a lane splits in two finer ones from this raise (+0.3 x its own number)]; streak = a value streak's length [m least, most]; tine = [a lane's own threshold on the rib's whiteness (+-), its slant across the lane]: the white's, the gold's and the amber's ends are tines along the sweep, never a line across; cut = the whiteness at which [amber turns gold, gold turns white]; comb = a lane starts at its own whiteness up to this (the tail's comb tines; the lane on the tip's path whole: the comma's point); dry = a dry gap's cell along a lane [m least, most]. All anchored to the laid path's metres: nothing swims.

grip._doc_dry_out: (take 7, iii) leaving: the dry gaps' share of each lane by s since the contact (the last three drawn frames before retract's end: gaps open along the WHOLE length, the last frame mostly streaks). dry_tail = (take 8) before that, from the middle of the life: the share of some lanes that is dry gap at the drawn tail (none past the stroke's middle), by s since the contact. shed_white = leaving: [whiteness added along the tip's path (the white runs on), taken along the inner edge (the gold lies there)].

splay._doc: (take 7, iv) THE CONTACT SPLAYS: out = the pressed ribs' outer edge past the tip's path (a share of the blade at the raise's most); tines = [for one body, for a crowd (contact.by_struck[0])] short fanned tines rooted on the pressed section's outer edge (none for an air cut); len = a tine's length out [m least, most]; root = its half width at the root [PIXELS, take 8: hair-thin flicks, not thorns]; slant = its lean the travel's way [m along per m out]; frames = the tines' share by drawn frame since the contact (three press frames, then the outer edge is clean again).

throw._doc: (take 7, iv) THE PAINT REACHES THE CUT'S HIT RADIUS: thin streaks rooted on the pressed section's outer edge, thrown out from her inside the cut's arc toward the sim's reach (Ev.Slash.Reach), continuous lines of the stroke's own mesh and material (never specks). per_struck = streaks per DISTINCT body struck (at least one for a hit, none for an air cut), most = at most; px = a streak's half width at its root (PIXELS however far the sheet fans; never under a pixel wide); len = its length [least, most] as a share of the way from the tip's path to the reach; min = that way's least (m); slant = its lean the travel's way; (take 8) slant may run against the travel (they FAN past their radials); span = the roots' spread as a share of the contact's reaches; frames = its width by drawn frame since the contact (shed in three); a shed streak FLIES: fly = its near end's place by frame (share of its length: it leaves the root), dash = its dashes' share by frame, dash_m = a dash's cell (m), bend = its bend with the sweep (m along per m out at its end); color = a streak is white to this share of its length, gold after (never amber: a thin amber line over the ground read black).

white._doc: (take 7, vii) THE STROKE'S OWN WHITE (sRGB 0-1), not the steel family's cream core (her ground ring's): day, and night (take 8: WHITER than the ring's cream core, sRGB 1 / 0.90 / 0.59: the gold is the inner band's and the tail's, so the ring and the stroke are two things).

smear.what: a swept arc on the blade's path at its reach
